_about: Single source of truth for every rendering, and the auditable term ledger (check 5). ONE rendering per referent for the whole book. Before you romanize any name, check here. status per entry: 'attested' (an established English name, or a real person/place/thing confirmed against scholarship), 'provisional' (romanization mine, not found in outside sources; the builder appends a visible marker), 'decided' (a project style call, e.g. standard pinyin of a fictional name). REAL vs FICTIONAL: the novel's principals (Chen Qianli, Ling Wen, Yi Junnian, Fang Yunping, You Tianxiao, Mu Chuan, Ye Qinian, etc.) are the author's invention set against a real historical backdrop; entries marked 'attested' for real historical figures/places note that they are documented. Sections are rendered as glossary headings; keys starting with '_' are ignored.

卫达夫.note: Communist agent ('Old Wei'); a street-runner for a house-letting agency. Fictional.

易君年.note: Communist ('Old Yi'); Ling Wen's superior; keeps a painting-and-scroll shop. Fictional.

凌汶.note: Communist; writer, author of the novel Winter; a merchant's widow. Fictional.

秦传安.note: Communist; a doctor with his own clinic. Fictional.

田非.note: Communist; library clerk who found the hidden meeting room. Fictional.

崔文泰.note: A hired-car driver and Old Fang's courier; revealed in ch14 to be the mole 'Xi Shi,' who betrayed Old Fang to the enemy. Fictional.

林石.note: Communist; clerk at the Rentai Bank; shot in the leg during the arrest. Fictional.

梁士超.note: Prisoner; claims to have served in the Nineteenth Route Army; wounded fighting the encirclement campaigns. Fictional.

方云平.note: Communist ('Old Fang'); the Shanghai underground's local head; missed the meeting; the gunman on Pu'enjishi Road; killed at his son's barbershop. Fictional.

小方.note: Old Fang's son, a barber; taken in the raid on the barbershop. Fictional.

董慧文.note: Communist; young schoolteacher at Minghui Primary School; close to Chen Qianyuan. Fictional.

陈千元.note: Communist; a translator for a news agency; Chen Qianli's younger brother. Fictional.

陈千里.note: Communist operative, the novel's central figure; trained three years in the USSR; Chen Qianyuan's elder brother. Fictional.

老开.note: Alias of the Central Liaison Bureau man arrested at the meeting, who was to convey the secret task. Distinct from Haohan. Fictional.

李汉.note: A comrade whose elder brother died a martyr; named by Old Fang. Fictional.

老陆.note: Day-shift attendant at the Shenxin Hotel. Fictional.

金先生.note: A great Shanghai art collector in Yi Junnian's anecdote. Fictional.

龙冬.note: Ling Wen's late husband, killed in Guangzhou; his name echoes her novel's title Winter (冬). Fictional.

浩瀚.note: Working alias ('the vast') of a senior Communist leader the enemy is hunting. Fictional.

游天啸.note: Captain of the Longhua detective squad; secret man of the Party Affairs Investigation Section. Fictional.

穆川.note: Director of the garrison's Judge Advocate's office; You Tianxiao's nominal superior. Fictional.

叶启年.note: You Tianxiao's teacher; deputy director of the Special Operations Headquarters. Fictional.

马秘书.note: Ye Qinian's aide in Nanjing. Fictional.

姚探长.note: Chinese detective of the Settlement's Central Police Station. Fictional.

翁副官.note: A Cantonese staff officer about the Garrison Command. Fictional; distinct from the real Brigade Commander Weng.

翁照垣.note: Real. Weng Zhaoyuan (1892-1972) of the Nineteenth Route Army, who held Zhabei in the Jan 28 1932 fighting; invoked in Liang Shichao's cover story.

蔡军长.note: Real. The Nineteenth Route Army's general Cai Tingkai (蔡廷锴).

宋先生.note: The man arranging Miss Tao's release and marriage; with Mrs. Song (宋太太). Fictional.

陶小姐.note: A cellmate of Ling Wen and Dong Huiwen; released, and made to carry Ling Wen's letter. Fictional.

蒋介石.note: Real. Nationalist leader ('the Generalissimo,' 委员长); directing the anti-Communist campaigns from Nanchang in 1932-33.

委员长.note: Chiang Kai-shek, in his title as chairman of the Military Affairs Commission.

李国杰.note: Real. Grandson of Li Hongzhang; principal of the 1933 China Merchants embezzlement case, sentenced to eight years.

李鸿章.note: Real. Late-Qing statesman, founder of China Merchants; the 'Grand Secretary Li' (李中堂) of the gossip.

陈孚木.note: Real. A go-between in the China Merchants case.

杜月笙.note: Real. Shanghai Green Gang boss and Nationalist ally; the 'tycoon Du' (杜大亨).

慈禧太后.note: Real. The late-Qing regent; she gave Li Guojie an imperial guard's post.

徐枕亚.note: Real. Patriarch of the 'Mandarin Ducks and Butterflies' romance school (author of Yulihun); name-dropped by Miss Tao.

金焰.note: Real. Korea-born film star, the 'Emperor of Film'; led the Lianhua film Cuckoo Soul Abroad.

鲁迅.note: Real. The great writer, patron of the League of Left-Wing Writers; co-edited The Outpost and mourned the Longhua martyrs.

冯雪峰.note: Real. Left-wing critic and Party literary figure; co-edited The Outpost with Lu Xun.

陈赓.note: Real. Red Army commander and intelligence figure; met Lu Xun secretly in Shanghai in 1932.

孙中山.note: Real. 'Mr. Sun,' founder of the Republic; visited the Yihong Garden more than once in 1912-13.

玛琳·黛德丽.note: Real. German-American film star, of Shanghai Express (1932); on the Grand Theatre poster.

仇英.note: Real. Ming master painter, one of the Four Masters of the Ming; much forged.

吴四宝.note: Shares the name of a real figure (c.1904-1942): a racecourse groom turned chauffeur who rose through the Green Gang and later led the armed unit of the collaborationist 'No. 76' secret service. The novel's minor tenant ('Little Bao') borrows the man and his groom-to-driver rise; his role here is fictional.

吴作民.note: Wu Zuomin, assistant manager (襄理) at the Zhonghui Trust Bank; addressee of Lin Shi's coded letter. Fictional.

金德林.note: 'Young Jin,' a former street-runner at the house-letting agency once used as Yi Junnian's letter-drop; left the job last year. Fictional.

叶桃.note: Ye Qinian's daughter and Chen Qianli's love; already dead when the novel opens, her death (which Chen blames on her father) drives both men. First named in ch12. Fictional. Her given name 桃 ('peach') puns on the peach-blossom letter-paper.

小五子.note: The woman for whom Cui Wentai loses his head, part of what tips him into betrayal. Fictional.

少山.note: Real. 少山 was a genuine cover name of Zhou Enlai (周恩来) in the Shanghai underground (attested in the 1932 'Wu Hao Incident'). The novel uses it as the figure who routes Chen Qianli to the USSR; Zhou had in fact left Shanghai by late 1931, so the early-1933 scene is a compressed, literary use of the alias.

秦邦宪.note: Real. 'Bo Gu' (博古, 1907-1946), de facto head of the CCP's Provisional Central; his signed article in Red China signals to Ye Qinian that the Provisional Central was moving from Shanghai to Ruijin in early 1933.

陈立夫.note: Real. 'Mr. Lifu' (立夫先生, 1900-2001); with his brother Chen Guofu the boss of the KMT 'CC Clique,' head of the Central Organization Department over the Party Affairs Investigation Section; the man Ye Qinian works through at headquarters.

沙逊.note: Real. Sir Victor Sassoon, the magnate who built the Cathay Hotel / Sassoon House on the Bund; Ye Qinian pointedly lodges 'in Sassoon's own house.'

涅克拉索夫.note: Real. Nikolai Nekrasov (1821-1877), Russian poet; the brothers' countersign adapts a line from his early love lyric 'The Storm' (Burya).

小施.note: Safe-deposit clerk at the Zhonghui Trust Bank; passed off by Miss Tao as her cousin and placed in the bank by Mr. Song. Fictional.

纪先生.note: The wealthy-collector cover name under which Chen Qianli enters the bank vault in ch17. A Chen Qianli alias; fictional.

王金枝.note: The murdered Taikoo-steamer head steward of Cui Wentai's gold-bar anecdote; apparently the novel's invention (no such case is attested). Fictional.

陶希圣.note: Real. Tao Xisheng (1899-1988), a theorist of the Three Principles at National Central University from 1931; later ghostwrote Chiang Kai-shek's China's Destiny (1943). The 'Professor Tao of Central University' whose book Ye Qinian recommends; a specific 1933 anti-Communist primer by him is not documented.

宋子文.note: Real. Nationalist finance minister 1928-1933; evoked (unnamed) by the hint that 'Mr. Song's' elder brother is a great personage and the bank does Ministry of Finance bond business.

莫少球.note: 'Boss Mo,' proprietor of the Xingchang Apothecary and head of the Party's Guangzhou courier station. Fictional.

莫太太.note: Mo Shaoqiu's wife and comrade at the Guangzhou courier station; a former courier who once met the man she takes for Long Dong. Fictional.

老肖.note: A high-ranking secret courier of the Central Committee's Liaison Bureau, sent from the Ruijin Soviet with a secret oral order for Lin Shi. Fictional.

邓中夏.note: Real (1894-1933). Founding leader of the Chinese labor movement and a chief organizer of the Canton-Hong Kong Strike; lectured at the strike's Labour College; executed by the Nationalists at Yuhuatai, Nanjing, Sept 1933.

陈济棠.note: Real (1890-1954). The 'King of the Southern Sky,' militarist who ruled Guangdong semi-independently c.1929-1936; socially conservative regime.

朱晖日.note: Real. Director of the Guangzhou Municipal Public Security Bureau from Oct 1927; took part in suppressing the Dec 1927 Canton Uprising. Exact tenure in the early 1930s undocumented.

卢忠德.note: In Mrs. Mo's story, a comrade planted in the Guangzhou public-security bureau, shot when the network was broken. Apparently fictional.

欧阳民.note: 'Secretary Ouyang,' the special-committee secretary in Mrs. Mo's story. Apparently fictional.

柔石.note: Real (Zhao Pingfu, 1902-1931). Left-wing writer, author of the novella February; one of the Five Martyrs of the League of Left-Wing Writers, shot at Longhua 7 Feb 1931.

陶元庆.note: Real (1893-1929). Book-cover artist for Lu Xun; his line drawing was the actual cover of February (not the woodcut the novel describes).

七姑.note: 'Seventh Aunt,' the self-combed amah who minds the abandoned house on the Rear Street of Tianguan Li. Fictional.

廖仲恺.note: Real (1877-1925). Leading KMT leftist, finance minister of the Guangzhou government, champion of the Soviet/CCP alliance; assassinated in Guangzhou 20 Aug 1925.

戴季陶.note: Real (1891-1949). KMT theorist of anti-communism ('Daiism'); reread Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles to exclude the Communists.

冯玉祥.note: Real (1882-1948). Warlord whose Beijing Coup of 23 Oct 1924 seized the capital and detained President Cao Kun.

曹锟.note: Real (1862-1938). President of the Republic 1923-24, deposed and placed under arrest in Feng Yuxiang's 1924 coup.

缪莲仙.note: Real Qing literatus (缪艮), by tradition author of the Cantonese naamyam Ke Tu Qiu Hen; the attribution is disputed.

黎遂球.note: Real (1602-1646). Ming loyalist poet-general of Guangzhou; Haoxian Road was renamed 豪贤 to honor him.

工部局.note: Real. Governing body of the foreign-run International Settlement.

巡捕房.note: Real. The Settlement's police (and, by extension, a police station); the Central Station is 中央捕房.

侦缉队.note: The Longhua garrison's plainclothes criminal-investigation squad, under You Tianxiao.

军法处.note: Real. The garrison's military-justice department; its head (处长) is rendered 'Director'.

淞沪警备司令部.note: Real. The Shanghai-Woosung garrison HQ at Longhua; also 龙华警备司令部, 'the Longhua Garrison Command'; the site of the 1931 executions.

党务调查科.note: Real. Kuomintang political-intelligence organ; forerunner of the wartime Bureau of Investigation and Statistics (中统).

特工总部.note: Insiders' name for the Investigation Section's Nanjing base at the Zhanyuan.

中央组织部.note: Real. The Kuomintang organ over the Investigation Section.

中央交通局.note: The Party's clandestine courier and liaison organ; 'Old Kai' belonged to it.

十九路军.note: Real. Cantonese army that fought the Japanese at Shanghai in 1932, later sent against Communists in Fujian.

斧头帮.note: Shanghai assassins' gang; linked to the killing of the China Merchants director.

招商局.en: the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company
招商局.note: Real. Founded by Li Hongzhang; center of the 1933 embezzlement scandal.

向导.note: Real. The Chinese Communist Party's central organ of the 1920s; Haohan published in it.

前哨.note: Real. Organ of the League of Left-Wing Writers; its 1931 first issue mourned the Longhua martyrs.

左联.note: Real. The League of Left-Wing Writers (Shanghai, 1930); five members among the 1931 Longhua martyrs.

国际通讯社.note: Chen Qianyuan's workplace, translating wire dispatches.

申报.note: Real. The major Shanghai newspaper, founded 1872.

房屋经租处.note: A property-letting and rent-collecting office; Wei Dafu's cover, through which safe houses were rented.

南昌行营.note: Real. Chiang Kai-shek's field HQ (formally from May 1933) for the anti-Communist campaigns.

山卡罗氏歌剧团.note: Real. A touring Italian opera company; staging Turandot at the Carlton in the novel (the Shanghai run itself unconfirmed).

中汇信托银行.note: Real. The Zhonghui Bank (中汇银行), founded 1929 by the Green Gang boss Du Yuesheng; it had a real trust department and safe-deposit vault. 'Trust Bank' renders the novel's 信托银行.

仁泰银公司.note: Lin Shi's cover employer; a realistic native-bank name, unattested and likely fictional.

东陆经租处.note: Wei Dafu's employer, a house-letting agency (经租处). Fictional.

冠生园.note: Real. Famous Shanghai food-and-confectionery company (founded 1915 by Xian Guansheng), noted for pastries and mooncakes.

云禄车行.note: The car-hire firm ('Yunlu Motor-Hire') whose Buick You Tianxiao hires to enter the Settlement. Fictional.

红色中华.note: Real. Organ of the Chinese Soviet Republic's central government, first published at Ruijin on 11 Dec 1931; a copy of it is the enemy's clue that the Party center is at Ruijin.

工人纠察队.note: Real. The armed labor militia of the CCP-led Shanghai workers' uprisings of 1926-27; disarmed and massacred in Chiang's 12 April 1927 coup.

临时中央.note: Real. The CCP's Provisional Central (Politburo) run in Shanghai under Bo Gu; it relocated to the Central Soviet at Ruijin in early 1933.

裕记钱庄.note: The native bank half-funded by the Special Operations Headquarters, used as Ye Qinian's command post opposite the bank. Fictional.

南市警察署.note: Real institution. The Chinese-city police of Nanshi, one of Shanghai's three separate forces (with the Settlement's Municipal Police and the French Concession police); the Chinese municipal force was headquartered in Nanshi. The exact station name is the novel's label.

太古.note: Real. Butterfield and Swire; its China Navigation Company (founded 1872) ran Yangtze steamers Shanghai-Hankou. The 'Taikoo steamer' of Cui Wentai's anecdote.

济难会.note: Real. The China Relief Society (1925), reorganized as the China Red Aid Society (1929); Communist-led relief and legal aid, hiring lawyers to bail out arrested comrades. Banned 1934.

劳动学院.note: Real. Worker-education body run under the Canton-Hong Kong Strike committee, where Deng Zhongxia lectured; its siting in the Nanhua Building is the novel's detail.

公董局.note: Real. Conseil d'administration municipale, governing body of the Shanghai French Concession; distinct from the SMC (工部局) of the International Settlement.

先施公司.note: Real. The first modern Chinese-run department store (Ma Ying-piu; Hong Kong 1900, Guangzhou 1912, Shanghai 1917), famous for rooftop amusement parks.

广州民国日报.note: Real. Nationalist newspaper founded 1923, an early KMT party organ; renamed the Zhongshan Daily in 1937.

大美晚报.note: Real. The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, American-owned and foreign-registered; Chinese edition from 16 Jan 1933.

反省院.note: Real. Nationalist prison for 'reforming' captured Communists (from c.1929; Nanjing's Capital Reflection Institute chartered 1931).

国华报.note: Real privately-run Guangzhou daily; the novel's two-run (day/evening) publishing detail is uncorroborated.

广州报界公会.note: A press guild on Shibafu Street with an attached clipping bureau; local color.

龙华.note: Real. District southwest of Shanghai; seat of the garrison and its prison; site of the 1931 martyrs.

玄武湖.note: Real. Lake against the northeastern wall of Nanjing.

四马路.note: Real. Today Fuzhou Road; books, theaters, brothels, and the 1930 produce market.

三马路.note: Real. Today Hankou Road, parallel to Fourth Avenue.

浙江大戏院.note: Real. Hudec's cinema of c.1930 at 123 Zhejiang Middle Road, facing the Fourth Avenue market (the author's named location, not the later 大上海大戏院).

世界大旅社.note: A hotel topped by a roof-garden amusement ground (carousel, skating rink, billiards) over the Fourth Avenue market; such rooftop gardens were a real feature of the district. Sources consulted differ on whether this specific establishment is documented; distinct from the Great World (大世界).

大光明大戏院.note: Real. Shanghai's premier cinema; Hudec's Art Deco rebuild completed mid-1933.

卡尔登大戏院.note: Real. Theater on Park Road (today Huanghe Road).

兰心大戏院.note: Real. The Settlement's foreign theater, by its standing English name; 1931 building on today's Maoming Road S.

派克路.note: Real. Today Huanghe Road, off West Nanjing Road.

跑马场.note: Real. The Shanghai Race Club course (also 跑马厅); its grounds are today People's Square and People's Park.

跑马厅路.note: The road beside the Race Club.

四行储蓄会大楼.en: the Four Banks' Savings Society building
四行储蓄会大楼.note: Real. The Park Hotel (国际饭店), Hudec, completed 1934; long the tallest building in Asia.

马立斯大楼.note: 'Morriss' (马立斯) renders the British Morriss family (North-China Daily News); the specific building by the racecourse is not separately documented.

德国医院.note: Real. The Paulun Hospital (宝隆医院) in the Settlement; where Dr. Qin trained.

白云观.note: Real. 'White Cloud Temple,' a Daoist temple in the old Chinese city; used here as a detective-squad base.

同春坊.note: Lane running to the gate of the Gezhi school and Minghui Primary School.

格致公学.note: Real. English-style boys' school run by the Municipal Council; today Shanghai Gezhi High School.

苏州河.note: Real. The creek down which the market's produce is boated in.

金利源码头.note: Shanghai wharf; among those mortgaged in the China Merchants case.

报恩塔.note: Real. The ancient Longhua Pagoda (standardly 龙华塔); 'Bao'en Pagoda' is a traditional alternate name for it.

南市.note: Real. The old Chinese city south of the Settlement.

枫林桥.note: Landmark on the road out to Longhua.

老闸捕房.note: Settlement police station; Ling Wen is first held here.

南京路.note: Real. Shanghai's grand commercial street; opposed to grim Longhua.

徐家汇.note: Real. District with the postal sub-office named as the letter's drop.

普恩济世路.note: Shanghai street where Fang Yunping opened fire.

圣母院路.note: Shanghai street ('Convent Road') giving off Pu'enjishi Road.

小浜湾.note: A creek-bend and lane by Pu'enjishi Road.

申新旅社.note: The hotel where Chen Qianli lodges under his antiques-dealer cover.

北四川路.note: Real. Today Sichuan North Road; heart of the 1930s left-wing literary quarter in Hongkou.

公益坊.note: Real. Lane off North Sichuan Road, a node of left-wing publishing (Shuimo and Xinken bookshops).

扆虹园.note: Real. Cantonese garden-mansion in the North Sichuan Road area; visited by Sun Yat-sen in 1912-13.

下关.note: Real. Nanjing's riverside district and railway station on the Yangtze.

鸡鸣寺.note: Real. Temple by the Nanjing city wall, passed on the drive.

神策门.note: Real. Gate in the Ming wall of Nanjing.

瞻园.note: Real. Nanjing garden housing the Special Operations Headquarters.

明城墙.note: Real. The great Ming-dynasty wall of Nanjing, along Xuanwu Lake.

新京.note: Real. 'New Capital,' Manchukuo's capital, today Changchun.

满洲国.note: Real. The Japanese puppet state in the occupied Northeast, proclaimed 1932.

北平.note: Real. Beijing's name in 1928-49; source of the evacuated Palace Museum treasures.

山海关.note: Real. Great Wall pass at the sea, taken by Japan Jan 1933.

伯力.note: Real. City in the Soviet Far East; site of Chen Qianli's training school.

海参崴.note: Real. Soviet Pacific port on Chen Qianli's route home.

青岛.note: Real. Port where the unexpected visitor boards Chen Qianli's ship.

吴淞口.note: Real. The mouth of the Huangpu at the Yangtze estuary off Shanghai.

故宫博物院.note: Real. The Beiping museum whose treasures were evacuated south in 1933.

马立斯新村.note: The lane-house estate where Ling Wen sublets; the Morriss name (see the Morriss Building) is attested, this specific estate the novel's setting.

虹口公园.note: Real. The largest public park of foreign Shanghai, in Hongkou; today Lu Xun Park (鲁迅公园). Site of the 29 April 1932 Yun Bong-gil bombing.

静安寺.note: Real. Ancient Buddhist temple on Bubbling Well Road (today Nanjing West Road); famed for the New Year 'first incense.'

同福里.note: The lane housing Qin Chuan'an's clinic; a realistic but unattested Shanghai lilong name. Likely fictional.

三成坊.note: Sub-lane of Tongfu Li at the clinic; realistic but unattested. Likely fictional.

田谷邨.note: A new-style lilong on the real Yuyuan Road; unattested by that name (echoes the actual 愚谷邨, Yugu Cun). Street and building type are real.

愚园路.note: Real. Exclusive residential road in western Shanghai; still Yuyuan Road.

地丰路.note: Real. Rue Tifeng; today Urumqi North Road (乌鲁木齐北路).

海格路.note: Real. Avenue Haig (after Field Marshal Douglas Haig); today Huashan Road (华山路).

善钟路.note: Real. Rue Say Zoong, the sole French Concession road named for a Chinese (the land magnate Tao Shanzhong); today Changshu Road (常熟路).

赵主教路.note: Real. Route Monseigneur Maresca, after the Catholic bishop of Nanjing Francesco Maresca (赵方济); today Wuyuan Road (五原路).

马斯南路.note: Real. Rue Massenet, after the composer Jules Massenet; today Sinan Road (思南路). The recognition-signal address.

肇嘉浜.note: Real. A commercial/industrial creek lined with wharves and yards in the 1930s; filled in 1954-56 to become Zhaojiabang Road.

提篮桥监狱.note: Real. The 'Ward Road Gaol' in Hongkou, built by the International Settlement and opened 1903; long one of the largest prisons in the Far East ('Far East's No. 1 prison').

华懋饭店.note: Real. Victor Sassoon's Art Deco hotel on the Bund (Sassoon House, opened 1929); today the north building of the Peace Hotel (和平饭店). Its revolving door gives the chapter its title.

澄衷中学.note: Real. School in Hongkou founded 1900 by the merchant Ye Chengzhong (叶澄衷); still exists as Shanghai Chengzhong High School.

下海庙.note: Real. A popular folk temple in the Tilanqiao area of Hongkou.

新闸路.note: Real. Shanghai road where Ye Qinian's old lane house (and its anarchist salon) stood in Chen Qianli's student days; still Xinzha Road.

仁记路.note: Real. Jinkee Road, a narrow street of foreign-firm buildings behind the Bund (today part of Dianchi Road).

外滩.note: Real. Shanghai's riverfront boulevard of foreign banks and hotels along the Huangpu.

黄浦江.note: Real. The river through Shanghai; the Bund runs along its west bank.

董家渡.note: Real. A riverside district of the old Chinese city (Nanshi), south of the Settlement.

奉贤.note: Real. Coastal county south of Shanghai, with reed marshes by the sea where Old Fang taught Cui Wentai to shoot.

瑞金.note: Real. Town in Jiangxi, capital of the Central Soviet and of the Chinese Soviet Republic; the Party center relocated there in early 1933.

天津路.note: Real. Street in the old International Settlement just north of Nanjing Road; a real hub of banks and native banks, one of Shanghai's 'bank streets.'

熙华德路.note: Real. Hongkou street built 1864, named for an American consul; renamed Changzhi Road (长治路) in 1943.

江西路.note: Real. North-south street a block back from the Bund, in the financial district; Yi Junnian's Nanshi-police car waits there.

阜成里.note: The lane opposite the Zhonghui Trust Bank; the enemy's command post is inside it and the underground's pickup cafe at its mouth. Realistic but unattested; likely fictional.

逸园咖啡馆.note: The cafe at the mouth of Fucheng Li, the underground's pickup point; a small bank-district cafe, distinct from the famous 逸园 Canidrome dog track. Likely fictional.

汕头.note: Real. Guangdong port; the sea link on the CCP's 'Central Red Route' courier line (Shanghai-Hong Kong-Shantou-Dabu-Ruijin), whose Shanghai-Shantou leg the group is to rebuild.

武汉.note: Real. The tri-city Yangtze port (Hankou/Wuchang/Hanyang); the upriver end of the gold-carrying steward's run in Cui Wentai's anecdote.

杭州.note: Real. Site of the secret-service training class You Tianxiao attended under Ye Qinian.

茂昌煤号.note: Coal firm on the Zhaojiabang whose Chinese-side coal yard the group uses as a refuge; worker Li Han's employer. Fictional.

兴昌药号.note: Apothecary in Xirong Lane, Xiguan, Guangzhou, run by the Party as a liaison station. Fictional.

添男茶楼.note: Teahouse with a round white roof on Yang Lane, Guangzhou, a landmark by the liaison station (and ch22's title). Local color, apparently fictional.

南华楼.note: Building with the Xinya Hotel at Xihaokou, Taiping South Road, Guangzhou; the novel puts the strike-era Labour College on its fourth floor. Setting; the Labour College placement is unconfirmed.

沙面.note: Real. Pearl-River islet made into British and French concessions after 1859; from it Anglo-French troops fired on marchers across the Shakee Canal, 23 June 1925.

大沙头.note: Real. Guangzhou's eastern railway station (built 1911), terminus of the Canton-Kowloon line; renamed Guangzhou East Station in 1947.

顾家宅公园.note: Real. The French Concession's park (Parc de Koukaza), opened 1909; today Fuxing Park.

平民宫.note: Real. Shelter for the poor completed in Guangzhou 1931 under Chen Jitang; funded from seized smuggler money (the novel says opium-boat fines).

浆栏街.note: Real. Street of apothecaries in the Xiguan district of Guangzhou.

双门底.note: Real. Historic site of Guangzhou's New-Year flower market; today's Beijing Road.

高第街.note: Real. Old commercial street in Guangzhou.

豪贤路.note: Real Guangzhou street near the Xiaobei Gate; older name 濠弦街 ('Moat-Bowstring Street'), for the moat it ran along.

光复路.note: Real Guangzhou street, here lined with newspaper offices.

十八甫.note: Real Xiguan market-street; 甫 denotes an old commercial street-market. Xiajiufu (下九甫) is another of the same family.

天官里.note: The lane and its Rear Street (后街) crime scene are the novel's invention, set on the real Haoxian Road. Fictional.

骰子.note: The pair of dice: the group's recognition sign, and the thread the enemy has hold of.

牌九.note: Domino gambling game; the cover for the meeting.

阴丹士林.note: Brand of colorfast synthetic dye; the blue of the schoolboys' gowns.

旗袍.note: The fitted dress; Miss Tao's, with the letter in its lining.

危害民国紧急治罪法.en: the Emergency Law for Crimes Endangering the Republic
危害民国紧急治罪法.note: Real. 1931 Nationalist law; carried the death penalty, used against Communists.

西施.note: Legendary beauty of Yue sent to ruin Wu; here the code name of a planted agent.

五卅运动.note: Real. 1925 anti-imperialist upheaval after Settlement police shot demonstrators.

一·二八.note: Real. The 1932 Battle of Shanghai against the Japanese.

大红袍.note: 'Great Red Robe,' the most prized of the Wuyi rock teas.

训政.note: The Nationalist 'tutelage' period of one-party rule.

特务工作之理论与实际.en: The Theory and Practice of Secret-Service Work
特务工作之理论与实际.pinyin: Tewu gongzuo zhi lilun yu shiji
特务工作之理论与实际.note: The scarce secret-service manual Mu Chuan asks You to bring.

冬.note: Ling Wen's (fictional) novel; Dong Huiwen has read it.

蓝钢快车.note: The overnight express between Shanghai and Nanjing.

青天白日旗.en: the Blue Sky and White Sun flag
青天白日旗.note: The Nationalist emblem flown over the garrison gate.

党国.note: Nationalist formula fusing party and nation.

围剿.note: Real. The Nationalist campaigns against the Communist base areas from 1930.

中央苏区.note: Real. The main Communist base area in Jiangxi-Fujian, capital Ruijin.

白区.note: Real. Nationalist-controlled territory, opposed to the 'Red'/Soviet areas; the underground's world.

南昌起义.note: Real. The Communists' 1 Aug 1927 revolt; founding day of the Red Army.

广州起义.note: Real. The Canton Uprising of Dec 1927 ('Guangzhou Commune').

大革命.note: Real. The 1924-27 National Revolution and First United Front, broken by Chiang in 1927.

远方来信.note: Real. Lenin's 1917 work, quoted by Chen Qianyuan; also the title of a later chapter.

未完成交响曲.note: Real. Schubert's Symphony No. 8 in B minor, rehearsed by the orchestra Dr. Qin watches.

图兰朵.note: Real. Puccini's last opera, set in a legendary Peking.

大香槟.note: Real. The Shanghai Race Club's sweepstakes lottery.

笑林广记.note: Real. The best-known classical Chinese joke-book, of the Qing dynasty.

明四家.en: the Four Masters of the Ming
明四家.note: Real. Shen Zhou, Wen Zhengming, Tang Yin and Qiu Ying.

茄力克.note: A British cigarette brand; also the title of a later chapter.

石库门.note: Shanghai stone-gate row houses; the barbershop lane is of this kind.

铺保.note: A merchant's guarantee standing bail for a prisoner's release.

二房东.note: A sub-lessor who leases a whole house and sublets rooms at a profit; a stock Shanghai figure. Ling Wen's cover.

四一二.note: Real. Chiang Kai-shek's 12 April 1927 purge of Communists in Shanghai, which shattered the First United Front and drove the Party underground.

老布尔什维克.note: A veteran who joined the Party in its earliest years; a mark of Yi Junnian's seniority.

水门汀.note: Shanghainese transliteration of English 'cement' (concrete); '水门汀 houses' are cement/reinforced-concrete buildings.

巴拉莱卡.note: The Russian triangular-bodied string instrument; the busker's song is the Yiddish folk song 'Tumbalalaika.'

第三次反围剿.note: Real. The Red Army's autumn-1931 defeat of the KMT's third 'encirclement and suppression' campaign in the Central Soviet.

邋遢冬至清爽年.en: A muddy Winter Solstice, a clear New Year
邋遢冬至清爽年.note: A Jiangnan weather proverb: an overcast Winter Solstice is taken to foretell a fine New Year, and vice versa.

亭子间.note: The small, cheap back room over the kitchen landing of a Shanghai lane house; the classic lodging of 1930s left-wing writers ('tingzijian writers').

世界语.note: The constructed universal language, championed by Chinese anarchists as a coming single world tongue; the cause of Ye Qinian's student salon.

朵云轩.note: Real. Shanghai studio (founded 1900) for fine paper and painting supplies, famed for woodblock-printed decorated letter-paper.

特派员.note: A special envoy sent by a higher Party organ to direct an operation; the enemy takes Lin Shi for one.

北伐.note: Real. The Nationalist-Communist military campaign (1926-28) from Guangzhou to unify China; its approach to Shanghai in 1927 is the backdrop to Cui Wentai's story.

废历.note: Real. The Nationalists' dismissive term for the lunar calendar they tried to suppress; hence '废历除夕,' the Eve of the Abolished Calendar.

大黄鱼.note: Old-Shanghai slang for a ten-tael gold bar (a one-tael bar was a 小黄鱼, 'little yellow croaker'); Cui Wentai's 'five big yellow croakers' are the five gold bars.

貂爪仁.note: Fur said to be pieced from the skin below a marten's claws; dramatizes the real furrier practice of piecing a garment from small prime parts of many pelts, but this specific category is unattested and likely the novel's embellishment.

钱庄.note: Real. The traditional Chinese private banking house, forerunner of the modern bank; distinct from the modern 银行.

估衣铺.note: Real. A shop dealing in used clothing, including fine robes let out to those wanting to look wealthy; Chen Qianli rents his rich-man's outfit from one.

简任.note: Real. Second-highest of the four Nationalist civil-service grades (特任/简任/荐任/委任); the Investigation Section chief's power far exceeds his middling jianren rank.

八七会议.note: Real. Emergency CCP conference, Hankou, 7 Aug 1927; set the line of land revolution and armed struggle after the First United Front collapsed.

省港大罢工.note: Real. The 1925-26 general strike and anti-British boycott in solidarity with the May Thirtieth Movement; Yi Junnian was in Guangdong for it.

三民主义.en: the Three Principles of the People
三民主义.note: Real. Sun Yat-sen's doctrine (Nationalism, Democracy, People's Livelihood); official ideology of the Nationalist state, invoked by Ye Qinian as the belief to replace Communism.

共产主义ABC.note: Real. Bukharin and Preobrazhensky's 1919 primer on the Bolshevik program, read in Chinese as an introduction to Communism; one of the books said to have 'turned' the young Chen Qianli.

中央红色交通线.note: Real. The enduring CCP courier line Shanghai-Hong Kong-Shantou-Dabu-Ruijin (from 1930), which moved documents, funds and 200+ cadres into the Central Soviet; the group is to rebuild the Shanghai-Shantou leg.

二月.note: Real. Rou Shi's 1929 novella, published by the Chunchao Book Company with a Lu Xun preface; the book Ling Wen buys, and this chapter's title.

吊钟花.note: Real. Enkianthus quinqueflorus, a traditional Cantonese Lunar New Year flower sold at the Guangzhou flower market.

竹筒屋.note: Real. Old Guangzhou townhouse, narrow-fronted and very deep, rooms strung front to back like the joints of bamboo.

满洲窗.note: Real. Lattice windows set with colored, etched glass, a signature of Xiguan houses in Guangzhou.

骑楼.note: Real. Lingnan shophouse whose upper floors overhang the pavement on columns to shelter it.

豪密.note: Real. Code devised by Zhou Enlai, named for his alias Wu Hao (伍豪); a code-book cipher, held never to have been broken.

煨灶猫.note: Wu-dialect idiom: a cat drowsing by the kitchen fire, i.e. a listless, spiritless person. Chen turns it around: 'the stove-cat turns into a tiger.'

趟栊门.note: The Cantonese three-part front door: swinging half-height 脚门, the sliding round-bar 趟栊, and the solid 大门. Ventilation plus security. The ch21 title.

自梳女.note: A Pearl-River-Delta woman sworn to lifelong spinsterhood; many became domestic amahs (妈姐).

疍家.note: The boat-dwelling 'water people' of the Pearl River and Guangzhou's creeks; a Tanka sampan carries the wounded Old Xiao away.

客途秋恨.note: Real Cantonese naamyam ('Autumn Lament of a Traveler'), sung on the teahouse stage in ch22.

黄大仙.note: Real Daoist immortal; drawing his oracle-lots (求签) is a genuine practice, though the novel's lot-73 verse is invented.

火水.note: Cantonese for kerosene; the northern Ling Wen does not know the word.
